subject: Dedicated safety-net & hyperscaler gap validation — next steps
messages:
From: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@aurorahealth.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: Priya Das <priya.das@aurorahealth.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Next steps after today's deep-dive (Dedicated vs hyperscaler)

Mina — thanks again for the demo today. Priya and I walked through Redwood's Dedicated offering and had two quick follow-ups before we take this internally to infra/security: 

1) Test scope: we want a concrete list of tests that will show differences vs our hyperscaler plan (reserved GPU VMs + autoscaling). Priority items for us are preemption behavior under sustained load, cold-start + warm cache recovery, and true tail latency (p95/p99) under mixed short/long prompt workloads.

2) SLA / safety net: if we commit to reserved capacity with a spike window, how would Redwood handle an unexpected region outage? We need a fallback path to a lower-cost hyperscaler pool or multi-region failover and clear runbook / RTO numbers.

3) Pricing/commitment clarity: what unit economics change when we add burst capacity vs fixed reservation? Can you share a sample ramp schedule and how discounts scale?

4) Evidence: SOC2 audit artifacts and a short comparison matrix that shows behavior we can present to our infra team.

Would you be able to share a short written test plan and a gap matrix we can include in our vendor review doc? We can kick off a 2-week validation window as early as Aug 2.

Thanks — Alex
---
Alex Rivera
Head of ML Infrastructure, Aurora Health AI
alex.rivera@aurorahealth.ai
+1 (415) 555-0182

From: mina_haddad@redwood.ai <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@aurorahealth.ai>
Cc: Priya Das <priya.das@aurorahealth.ai>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 21 Jul 2027 17:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps after today's deep-dive (Dedicated vs hyperscaler)

On Wed, Jul 21, 2027 at 3:12 PM Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@aurorahealth.ai> wrote:
> Mina — thanks again for the demo today. Priya and I walked through Redwood's Dedicated offering and had two quick follow-ups before we take this internally to infra/security: 
>
> 1) Test scope: ...

Thanks Alex — great questions and very much in line with what other infra teams ask. High level recap below and attached is a concise gap matrix (redwood-hyperscaler-gap-matrix.xlsx) plus a proposed test-case doc (proposed-test-cases.md).

Proposed validation buckets (we'll own setup + simple scripts, you run the attestation tests):
- Baseline latency/throughput: steady-state 8-hour run at target QPS with p50/p95/p99, token/sec, and GPU utilization.
- Preemption/resilience: simulate GPU preemption (node eviction) and measure RTO, request failover behavior, and any client-visible errors.
- Cold-start and KV/Warm-cache recovery: restart a model host and measure first-response latency and throughput for cached prefixes vs cold prompts.
- Mixed fanout: short chats (avg 40 tokens) + long completions (avg 800 tokens) to capture batching impact and tail latencies.
- Forced-burst: trigger 2x expected QPS for 15 minutes to validate autoscale/burst cushions and queueing/backpressure semantics.

Fallback/runbook options we recommend:
- Cross-region Dedicated standby: replicate model instances in a second region (adds cost but deterministic RTO).
- Hybrid fallback: automated routing to a verified hyperscaler pool when Dedicated capacity is exhausted; Redwood can enforce model parity (same quantization profile) and tag these requests for cost/quality tracing.

Pricing/commit comments:
- Reserved capacity covers baseline throughput; burst is billed as metered spend with explicit per-GPU-hour and per-token uplifts. We'll provide a sample ramp (attached).

Next steps / asks:
1) Confirm kickoff window Aug 2–Aug 13 (2-week validation).
2) Provide a target QPS profile and critical test prompts you want preserved for quality/regression checks.
3) Approve inclusion of a small test token spike to exercise fallback routing.

Attachments: redwood-hyperscaler-gap-matrix.xlsx (spreadsheet), proposed-test-cases.md (markdown)

I'll loop Sean for SLA/fallback detail and Marissa on the ops playbook.

Best,
Mina Haddad
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
mina_haddad@redwood.ai

From: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: mina_haddad@redwood.ai
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@aurorahealth.ai>
Date: Thu, 22 Jul 2027 09:18:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps after today's deep-dive (Dedicated vs hyperscaler)

Mina / Alex — quick internal / show-n-tell notes.

Mina: good plan. Couple of operational points to include in the runbook and test checklist: 
- SLA exception language: add an explicit "burst cushion" clause (e.g., x% guaranteed burst for y minutes) and a defined process for credits if fallback is used due to regional outage.
- Observability hooks: ensure we surface token-level origin (dedicated vs fallback) and per-request latency tags so their security team can audit permutations.
- Preemption metrics we should capture: number of evicted kernels, time-to-reconcile KV cache across hosts, and impact on long-running streams.

Alex: for pricing transparency we can provide a table mapping committed GPU-hours to effective per-million-token cost including quantized model profiles. We'll also include an example contract amendment for burst credits.

I'll draft the SLA appendix and share by EOD tomorrow. For the kickoff lab we should ask Aurora for a prioritized test list (3 must-have prompts and 2 regression prompts) so we keep the window tight.

—Sean
Sean Gallagher
Head of Revenue Operations, Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai

From: Priya Das <priya.das@aurorahealth.ai>
To: Mina Haddad <mina_haddad@redwood.ai>
Cc: Alex Rivera <alex.rivera@aurorahealth.ai>, sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 23 Jul 2027 09:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Next steps after today's deep-dive (Dedicated vs hyperscaler)

Thanks Mina / Sean — this is helpful. We reviewed the matrix and the proposed tests; Aurora can commit to Aug 2 kickoff. Confirming the asks from our side:

- Target QPS: baseline 120 req/s (mixed profile: 70% short, 30% long) with peak bursts to 240 req/s for 15 minutes.
- Must-have prompts: 3 short classification prompts (privacy-sensitive examples removed) and 2 long free-form summarization prompts.
- SOC2 artifacts: please share the auditor contact / report stub we can include in procurement package.

We approve hybrid fallback as the preferred safety net if you can provide documented RTO for cross-region failover and a clear cost delta for fallback usage.

I'll drop the prompt bundle and a short internal vendor memo to your Drive link today.

Best — Priya
Priya Das
Director, Platform Engineering, Aurora Health AI
priya.das@aurorahealth.ai
